target.title: fix(feishu): bound stalled docx image URL reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users rendering or uploading Feishu docx images from remote URLs could have the docx workflow hang when the remote image response body stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Docx image URL reads now go through a Feishu-local remote image reader that applies the selected account's Feishu HTTP timeout as two targeted deadlines: a response-header deadline and a response-body idle deadline. It no longer uses the setting as a complete-operation download deadline, so healthy large image transfers that keep making progress are not cut off solely because total elapsed time exceeds the header timeout. File upload remote reads keep their existing behavior, so this stays scoped to docx image handling.

## User Impact

Feishu docx image processing now degrades through the existing error handling instead of blocking the whole document operation on a stalled remote image body. Account-specific Feishu timeout settings are honored for docx image response headers and stalled body reads without changing the Feishu config schema.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/docx.test.ts` passed: 20 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/feishu/src/docx.ts extensions/feishu/src/docx.test.ts` passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/feishu/src/docx.ts extensions/feishu/src/docx.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Selected-account timeout proof: `feishu_doc` write with `resolveFeishuToolAccount(...).config.httpTimeoutMs = 1234` now calls `readRemoteMediaBuffer` with `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 1234` and `readIdleTimeoutMs: 1234` for the markdown image URL.
- Exact-head local media runtime proof at `28db697a9e527f82a196c7370fb1774691551f85`: the shared media reader was run against a local HTTP image server with the same deadline shape used by the Feishu docx image path. The body-stall case sent response headers and left the body open, then failed through `MediaFetchError`; the slow-progress case used `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 60` and kept sending chunks for 529ms, proving there is no complete-operation deadline cutting off a healthy transfer that continues to make progress.

Command:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module - <<'JS'
# local HTTP image server + readRemoteMediaBuffer({ responseHeaderTimeoutMs, readIdleTimeoutMs }) harness
JS
```

Redacted transcript:

```json

  "exactHead": "28db697a9e527f82a196c7370fb1774691551f85",
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:<redacted>",
  "options": "docx image path now passes responseHeaderTimeoutMs plus readIdleTimeoutMs, not timeoutMs",
  "cases": [
    {
      "name": "body-stall",
      "outcome": "threw",
      "elapsedMs": 271,
      "errorName": "MediaFetchError",
      "errorMessage": "Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:<redacted>/body-stall.png: Media download stalled: no data received for 80ms",
      "code": "fetch_failed"
    },
    {
      "name": "slow-progress",
      "outcome": "completed",
      "elapsedMs": 529,
      "bytes": 67,
      "contentType": "image/png"
    }
  ],
  "events": [
    { "route": "body-stall", "phase": "request-start", "method": "GET", "url": "/body-stall.png" },
    { "route": "body-stall", "phase": "headers-sent" },
    { "route": "body-stall", "phase": "body-stall", "note": "response body intentionally left open" },
    { "route": "slow-progress", "phase": "request-start", "method": "GET", "url": "/slow-progress.png" },
    { "route": "slow-progress", "phase": "headers-sent" },
    { "route": "slow-progress", "phase": "chunk", "bytes": 8 },
    { "route": "slow-progress", "phase": "chunk", "bytes": 16 },
    { "route": "slow-progress", "phase": "chunk", "bytes": 24 },
    { "route": "slow-progress", "phase": "chunk", "bytes": 19 },
    { "route": "slow-progress", "phase": "response-end" }
  ]
}
```

- Not run: live Feishu tenant / real Feishu doc upload.

AI-assisted change.
